points: The Sep-quarter results will show whether iPhone demand stayed strong after reports suggest the prior quarter posted a 22% sales jump; a sustained shipment trend supports the long, while a demand drop would undercut the recent upward estimate revisions.

Gross margin and services margin in the print will reveal how much memory-chip shortages and higher component costs are pressuring profitability; reports suggest shortages won't ease soon, so any margin resilience supports the long.

Guidance for the holiday quarter and early FY2027 will test whether the ~18.1% FY1 EPS growth and ~8.2% FY2 growth are still achievable under new CEO John Ternus; guidance that keeps FY2 from compressing supports the long.

Commentary on AI product integration and on-device intelligence should clarify whether Apple has a near-term hardware or services catalyst beyond the iPhone cycle; a credible roadmap supports the long.
China and regional revenue trends in the Sep quarter will show whether global consumer electronics demand remains firm; strength there supports the long and fits the theme's active lean-long stance.
Peer prints from SONO on Oct 26, GRMN and MSFT on Oct 28 arrive just before AAPL and may offer demand/supply read-throughs, while ROKU on Nov 6 follows as a check on consumer spending.
watch: 30-day analyst revisions: 21 up vs 8 down — supports the long if the Oct 30 report and guidance extend the upward revision trend.
FY1/FY2 EPS growth: ~18.1% followed by ~8.2% — supports the long if guidance does not push FY2 growth lower.
